items.prompt: What word do you get if you change the middle (vowel) sound in 'hot' from /o/ to /i/?

How many sounds are in 'string'?
A) 4
B) 5
C) 6

steps: Segment: /s/ - /t/ - /r/ - /i/ - /ng/. 'ng' is one sound. That is 5 sounds total.

items.prompt: Say the word 'blend'. Now say it without the /l/ sound. What new word do you get?

Which pair of words has the SAME vowel sound?
A) 'bit' and 'bite'
B) 'bit' and 'hit'
C) 'bite' and 'kite' — which pair has the same LONG vowel?
items.answer: C) 'bite' and 'kite' share the long /i/ sound.

steps: 'bit' has a short /i/ sound. 'bite' has a long /i/ sound — different.
'bit' and 'hit' both have short /i/ — same, but these are short vowels.
'bite' and 'kite' both have long /i/ — same long vowel sound.

items.prompt: Segment ALL the sounds in 'splash'. How many sounds does it have?
What word do you get if you swap the LAST sound in 'tap' from /p/ to /n/?
How many syllables does 'refrigerator' have? Clap it out.

steps: Clap: re (1) - frig (2) - er (3) - a (4) - tor (5). 'refrigerator' has 5 syllables.

items.prompt: Say 'sleep'. Now say it without the /l/. What word do you get?

Which word has 5 sounds?
A) shop (/sh/-/o/-/p/ = 3)
B) blend (/b/-/l/-/e/-/n/-/d/ = 5)
C) chip (/ch/-/i/-/p/ = 3)
Listen: /k/ - /l/ - /aw/ - /d/. Blend these sounds. What word is it?

steps: /k/-/l/-/aw/-/d/ blended together makes 'clawed'. The /aw/ is the vowel sound in 'clawed'.

items.prompt: What word do you get if you change the FIRST sound in 'bring' from /b/ to /sp/?

How many sounds are in 'cheese'?
A) 3
B) 4
C) 5

steps: Segment: /ch/ - /ee/ - /z/. 'ch' is one sound, 'ee' is one sound, 'z' (from 'se') is one sound. Total: 3 sounds.

items.prompt:
Which word pair are both long-vowel words?
A) 'cape' and 'cap'
B) 'cape' and 'game'
C) 'cap' and 'gap'

steps: 'game' also has the long /ay/ sound (a-e pattern).
So 'cape' and 'game' are both long-vowel words.

items.prompt: Say 'stamp'. Now remove the /t/. What word do you get?
A student says that 'dream' and 'cream' rhyme. Is the student correct? Explain using sounds.
items.answer: Yes. Both words end with the /eem/ sound: dr-EAM and cr-EAM.

steps: Because both endings sound the same, the words rhyme. The student is correct.
